Source: Core Rulebook, p. 310–311

When you give a Non-Player Character one of these spells, rename it and tweak its effects to suit your needs. Most spells are already customizable, allowing you to choose between status effects or damage types — you make this choice when you are designing your NPC.

For instance, you might give a creature Cursed Breath from the list below, choose ice damage and the slow status effect and rename it to Frozen Spear.

Area Status20SpecialInstantaneous
Every enemy the NPC can see suffers (choose one: dazed, shaken, slow, weak).

The NPC deals (HR + 10) (choose type) damage to the target.

The target suffers (choose one: dazed, shaken, slow, weak).

The target suffers (choose two: dazed, shaken, slow, weak).
Cursed Breath O10One creatureInstantaneous
The NPC deals (HR + 15) (choose type) damage to the target, then the target suffers (choose one: dazed, shaken, slow, weak).
Devastation30SpecialInstantaneous
The NPC deals 30 (choose type) damage to every enemy they can see. This spell should only be given to champion and elite enemies level 30 or higher, which should only cast it during their last turn of the round, creating a predictable pattern that Players can anticipate.
Lick Wounds5SelfInstantaneous
The NPC recovers 20 Hit Points. This amount increases to 30 Hit Points if the NPC is level 20 or higher, 40 Hit Points if they are level 40 or higher, or 50 Hit Points if they are level 60 or higher.
Life Theft O10One creatureInstantaneous
The NPC deals (HR + 15) (choose type) damage to the target, then recovers an amount of Hit Points equal to half the total Hit Point loss suffered by the target.

The NPC deals (HR + 15) (choose type) damage to the target, then recovers an amount of Mind Points equal to half the total Hit Point loss suffered by the target.

See You Later and Unexpected Ally

These two skills are available as Benefit Pool picks in this campaign — one player each, no duplicates.

SEE YOU LATER

Source: Core Rulebook, Rogue Skills, p. 201

You may use an action and spend 1 Fabula Point to vanish from the current scene, reappearing whenever you want during a different scene in which another Player Character is present. Describe how you escaped and miraculously got there!

UNEXPECTED ALLY

Source: Core Rulebook, Orator Skills, p. 199

You may use an action and spend 1 Fabula Point to choose a non-hostile creature able to hear and understand you. If you do, that creature becomes helpful towards you so long as you are kind and respectful to them and your requests are reasonable.

INSPIRING PRESENCE (Heroic Skill — interacts with Unexpected Ally)

Source: Playtest Materials (ENG, June 2026), p. 13

Requirements: you must have mastered Orator.

Once per turn, when you use the My Trust in You Skill during an ally's Accuracy Check or Magic Check for an offensive spell (O), you may have that attack or spell deal 5 extra damage.

When you use the Unexpected Ally Skill on a creature, you may have that creature become a follower of your group until your group gains another follower. Followers are always willing to help the group in dangerous situations; during conflict scenes, they follow the rules for NPCs as Special Abilities in the Game Master's Booklet (page 17). Essentially, the NPC does not have a dedicated profile and is instead represented by a passive benefit for the group, or by an active or reactive benefit that can be used two or three times per conflict scene. The specific benefits granted by a follower are created together by the entire group, and the Game Master has final say on them.
